subject: Dedicated deployment isolation attribute matrix + attack-paths — SOC 2 / SIG request
messages:
From: Jessica Lin <jessica.lin@acme-health.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme-health.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated deployment — request for isolation attribute matrix and attack-path map

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the earlier phone call. Acme Health's audit team has asked us to supply two concise artifacts for the upcoming SOC 2/SIG review focused on our Dedicated deployment:

1) An "isolation attribute matrix" that lists each logical component (control plane, serving runtime, model cache, metrics pipeline, etc.), the isolation boundary (VPCs, subnets, security groups), data classification, and the mitigations (IAM, KMS, route tables).

2) A short attack-paths diagram/annotation that shows the most likely lateral movement / exfil scenarios and what controls (NW ACLs, egress filtering, KMS segregation, host hardening, SIEM alerting) would detect/mitigate them.

Can you deliver these as a two-page PDF + a simple Visio/diagram file by EOD Wednesday (2027-06-30)? Our security ops will review and may send a short follow-up.

I've attached the questionnaire excerpts to show the specific fields we need mapped (see: acme-questionnaire-annotated.pdf).

Thanks — if a 30-minute readout helps, please propose times.

— Jessica
Security Program Manager
Acme Health

Short answer: yes, we can produce both artifacts by EOD Wednesday. Plan below; owners are listed so you know who's accountable.

Deliverables and owners:
- Isolation attribute matrix (PDF + Excel): Kimberly will own compilation and controls mapping.
- Attack-paths diagram (PDF + VSDX): Mina will sketch the diagrams and call out detection controls.

Proposed timeline:
- Wed 09:00 PT: internal review of drafts (30m)
- Wed 13:00 PT: deliver PDFs and VSDX to you

If that works, I'll set the internal review calendar and share a readout invite for Thursday if you want a live walkthrough.

Quick clarifying Qs (so we scope appropriately):
1) Do you want per-region variants (we can do single-region US-West as representative), or one canonical diagram?
2) Any minimum requirements for labels in the Visio file (e.g., must include asset tags / environment IDs)?

Thanks — we'll iterate quickly.

Best,
Priyom Das

priyom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0173
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment — request for isolation attribute matrix and attack-path map

Team — attaching the first draft of the isolation attribute matrix. Key assumptions at the top of the sheet.

Notes / callouts from my review: 
- We will scope to a single primary region (us-west-2) unless they explicitly request multi-region variants; that keeps the matrix compact.
- Control plane is customer-dedicated control plane (Private deployment pattern) for Acme's Dedicated instance — explicit KMS keys per-tenant, CMKs stored in customer-managed key rings where requested.
- Serving runtime instances are in a tenant-isolated subnet pool; we use VGW + route policies to avoid cross-tenant peering.
- KV cache: Strictly ephemeral and encrypted in transit; if stored, we persist only with tenant-scoped encryption keys (see row: cache encryption).
- Egress: Block by default with allowlists; all allowed egress must be via NAT/Gateway with logging exported to the tenant SIEM ingestion stream.

Open items I flagged in the sheet:
- Whether Acme requires air-gapped images for their model packaging (they flagged a compliance checkbox in the questionnaire).
- Whether they require hardware HSM-backed signing for runtime images.

I've attached: isolation-attribute-matrix-draft.xlsx (workbook) and inline notes. I'll finish the PDF render tomorrow morning and hand to Priyom for distribution.

-- Kimberly
Head of Platform Security, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Lin <jessica.lin@acme-health.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, mina.haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment — request for isolation attribute matrix and attack-path map

Jessica — attaching the deliverables we discussed. Short summary below.

Attachments: redwood-isolation-attribute-matrix-v1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages) — canonical matrix for us-west-2 (covers control plane, serving runtime, KV cache, observability pipeline, and admin plane); attack-paths-sketch.vsdx (Visio) — three annotated paths (credential theft -> lateral move, misconfigured egress -> data exfil, compromised third-party CI -> image tamper).

Summary highlights:
- Network boundaries: Tenant-serving subnets are isolated via subscription-level VPCs, enforced with security groups and explicit route tables; control plane is reachable only over authenticated mTLS with mutual TLS per-tenant certs.
- Key management: Tenant CMKs (customer-managed where requested) and a strict key-usage policy: model artifacts encrypted at rest, KV cache encrypted in transit and at rest per-tenant when persisted.
- Egress control: Default deny; explicit allowlist. All egress flows pass through a gated NAT with proxy that emits metadata to our observability pipeline.
- Detection: All host telemetry, control-plane API audit logs, and egress flow logs stream to the tenant SIEM ingestion topic for 365-day retention. We call out the top 4 Sigma rules that map to the attack-paths.

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether Acme wants the HSM-backed key material option for the CMKs (this changes the architecture callout slightly).
- If you'd like a 30-minute walkthrough of the diagrams, we are available Thu 09:30 PT or Thu 15:00 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to feedback.

Best,
Priyom
From: Jessica Lin <jessica.lin@acme-health.com>

Cc: security@acme-health.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment — request for isolation attribute matrix and attack-path map

Priyom — wonderful, thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear artifacts. A couple quick follow-ups from our security ops review: 

1) Egress filtering: can you include the list of allowed destination categories (artifact registries, telemetry endpoints, KMS endpoints) and note whether FQDN allowlists are supported by your proxy?
2) SIEM ingestion: confirm that the tenant SIEM topic supports encrypted ingestion (TLS + auth) and that we can export to our Splunk instance via a secure forwarder.

If possible, can you add those two clarifications to the PDF and re-send? Otherwise Thu 09:30 PT works for the walkthrough.

— Jessica
